transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came because I feel flat inside. Even when my children come sit with me, or the sun is shining on my garden—things that ought to make me feel glad or comforted—I just don’t feel it. It’s like that part of me has shut off.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
Yes... I feel flat. My children can be sitting with me, and the sun can be on my garden, things that used to comfort me, but I just don't feel glad anymore. It's like that part of me has shut off.
Before this period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this?
I’m not sure. I can’t think of another time I felt depressed like this.
Did these feelings start after something stressful or upsetting happened in your life?
Yes. It started about two weeks ago, after my husband collapsed and the paramedics were working on him in our kitchen.
Do you feel hopeless?
I’m not sure what you mean by hopeless. I just know I don’t feel like myself anymore.
Have you had thoughts that life is not worth living?
I don’t know. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Have these feelings made it hard for you to manage your usual day-to-day activities?

Yes. I’ve stopped going to the senior center, and I can’t keep up with meals, errands, or even my calendar unless my daughter helps me. Mostly I stay in the house, and I don’t go into the kitchen unless somebody is with me.
Since this began, have you been feeling anxious or on edge?
Yes. When I’m in the house, I keep listening for every little sound. I check the hallway and the back door, and I just don’t feel safe being in the kitchen by myself anymore.
Do unwanted images or memories of your husband collapsing keep coming into your mind?
I’m not sure what you mean by images. I do think about what happened sometimes, but I haven’t noticed pictures coming into my mind on their own.
Do you ever feel as if your husband’s collapse is happening again right in front of you?
No, I don’t think so. I remember it and I worry about it, but it doesn’t feel like it’s happening again in front of me.
Have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself a lot?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been thinking of myself as worthless, no.
Have you been avoiding the kitchen because it reminds you of what happened to your husband?

Yes. I mostly avoid the kitchen unless someone is with me. My daughter has been having to help me with meals and errands, even keeping track of my calendar. I’ve stopped going to the senior center and mostly just stay in the house.
For most of the day lately, have you been feeling sad or down?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been upset, of course, but I can’t say I’ve noticed feeling sad most of the day.
Have you lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?
I think so. Even when my children sit with me, or I see the sun on my garden, I just feel flat inside. It’s like I can’t feel glad or comforted by things the way I used to.
Lately, have you been feeling sad?
I’m not sure I’d call it sadness. I’ve been upset, but I haven’t really noticed feeling sad most of the day.
Since this started, have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to my sleep.
Since this started, have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. I used to plan meals and keep my calendar straight, but now I’ll look at a grocery list or the senior-center schedule and my mind just goes blank. My daughter has to help me with simple decisions.
Since this started, have you had much less appetite?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to how much I’ve been eating.
Lately, have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m moving or talking slower than usual.
Since this started, have you had sudden surges of intense fear or panic?
I’m not sure what you mean by surges. I do get upset, but I haven’t really noticed sudden panic coming on.
